TMA 512 Hyperion® Series
Product catalog summary
Introduction to Thermomechanical Analysis (TMA)
Thermomechanical Analysis (TMA) is a technique for measuring dimensional changes in materials as a function of temperature and time under mechanical force. It is used in research, development, simulation input, and quality control for materials such as plastics, elastomers, thermosets, composites, adhesives, films, fibers, ceramics, glass, and metals.
Key Analysis Results
TMA provides insights into linear thermal expansion, coefficient of thermal expansion, glass transition temperatures, delamination, isostrain, creep and relaxation, stress/strain curves, phase transition and sintering temperatures, shrinkage steps and kinetics, softening points, and density and volumetric expansion changes.
Operating Principle
The TMA 512 Hyperion® uses a sensitive inductive displacement transducer (LVDT) to detect dimensional changes. It features interchangeable pushrods and sample holders for specific applications.
Instrument Features
Features include an LED status bar, touch display, compatibility with other NETZSCH instruments, flexible temperature range and atmosphere control, and a wide selection of sample holders.
Advanced Capabilities
Advanced capabilities include temperature-modulated TMA, Rate-Controlled Sintering (RCS), H₂Secure concept for hydrogen environments, and simultaneous measurement of force and displacement.
Applications and Benefits
The TMA 512 Hyperion® series offers precise control and measurement, suitable for various applications in material science and engineering, enhancing productivity and workflow efficiency.
Overview
The document provides an overview of software and methodologies in thermal analysis, focusing on TMA and its applications in polymers, ceramics, and composites. It highlights software tools for enhancing accuracy and efficiency.
Software Features
Features include Temperature-modulated TMA for polymer analysis, c-DTA® for simultaneous length and thermal effect analysis, Kinetics Neo for optimizing ceramic production, Proteus® Software for data management, and LabV® for digital workflows and AI assistance.
Applications and Case Studies
Case studies include anisotropic behavior in composites, specifying materials for electronics, heat-shrink tubing, biopolymers and moisture absorption, and relaxation in polymer films.
Key Data and Graphs
The document includes graphs and data tables illustrating thermal expansion, glass transition, and other thermal properties of materials under specific conditions.
Thermal Expansion of Insulation Material
Discusses the thermal expansion of polymer foams like EPS and EPP, noting that lower density foams have higher coefficients of thermal expansion while maintaining similar glass transition temperatures.
Densification of a Ceramic Green Body by Rate-Controlled Sintering
Describes sintering a ceramic green body using RCS, noting key temperature transitions and a 13.7% sintering step.
Comparison of the Visco-Elastic Properties of Fused Silica and Flat Glass
Compares the visco-elastic behavior of fused silica and flat glass, noting differences in stiffness and softening points.
Molten Salts – Analysis of the Thermophysical Properties of an NaNO3-KNO3 Mixture
Analyzes the NaNO3-KNO3 system for heat transfer and thermal energy storage, noting phase-transition temperatures and volume changes.
Unlimited Warranty
NETZSCH offers an Unlimited Warranty for their instruments, ensuring long-term reliability and value maintenance.
Technical Specifications of TMA 512 Hyperion®
Provides technical specifications for the TMA 512 Hyperion® series, including temperature range, measuring ranges, furnace types, heating/cooling rates, and atmosphere compatibility.

Hydrogen Research
Using H₂Secure
The H₂Secure concept developed by NETZSCH features a complete solution for conducting tests in environments with varying hydrogen concentrations while providing a maximum in safety. This flexibility is achieved through a comprehensive safety protocol embedded in the system, enabling seamless performance of complex oxidationreduction cycles and precise analysis of reaction kinetics and material behavior under different conditions.

Simultaneous Measurement of Force and Displacement Signal
The force acting on the specimen is generated electromagnetically. This ensures a quick response time for experiments with a changing load. A highly sensitive force sensor (digital resolution < 0.01 mN, max. force ±4 N*) continuously measures the force exerted via the pushrod and automatically readjusts it. This sets the NETZSCH TMA 512 Hyperion® apart from other instruments, which only use preset values.
